newsitem.title: GERMANY: Delors sees agreement on EMU pact in Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: Delors sees agreement on EMU pact in Amsterdam.

text.p: Former EU Commisison president Jacques Delors predicted that an agreement will be reached on a euro zone stability pact at next week's EU summit meeting in Amsterdam. a press report said.

In an interview with Germany's Der Spiegel magazine, released on Saturday ahead of publication, Delors said he believed Amsterdam would also agree a protocol setting out how economic policies in the euro area will be co-ordinated.
"The stability pact will first be ratified and secondly, a protocol to define the conditions under which member states' economic policies will be co-ordinated with each other," Delors said.
"Thirdly there will be a new contract about reforming European institutions, of which I do not expect much, with a chapter on employment policies," he added.
Delors added that a delayed launch of the European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) project beyond the January 1 1999 deadline would be disastrous.
"That would mean a collapse of European integration," he said.

The Amsterdam summit takes place on Monday and Tuesday, following a nervous week for the monetary union project as the French Socialist government calls for more attention to be addressed to unemployment.

The German-inspired stability pact, which would impose tough sanctions on countries that stray from budgetary discipline once the single currency is launched in 1999, was agreed in Dublin last December.

But, abiding by an election pledge to reorient the drive to European monetary union, French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin is demanding that Europe's single currency plans take Europe's 18 million jobless into account.
